more.title: Grass and clover can provide more than animal feed
more.summary: Growing leys—grass and clover—is nothing new in Swedish agriculture. But in the arable farming regions dominated by cereal production, leys are less common. One reason is that there needs to be a market for what is harvested.

more.title: In hottest summer on record, 2 in 3 Americans say climate change is increasing heat-related illnesses
more.summary: Nearly two-thirds of the American public say climate change is increasing the risk of respiratory diseases and heat- and insect-related illnesses, according to a new survey from the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) of the University of Pennsylvania.

more.title: When prepping for disaster, don't forget to pack your teddy bear

more.title: Robots grow and package lettuce year-round in Norway's fully automated farm
more.summary: Norway's first fully automated facility for vegetable production was put into operation last fall. This spring, the first products hit store shelves.

more.title: Scientists discover a mysterious new frog hiding in the Amazon
more.summary: Scientists discovered a new frog species in the flooded forests of the western Amazon, distinguishing it from nearly identical relatives through DNA and its unique call. Adenomera varcena highlights how much Amazonian biodiversity remains hidden even as habitat loss and climate change threaten these poorly understood species.

more.title: Museums on prescription: How cultural activities are becoming crucial to the public health debate

more.title: Toxic algae can pose a hidden danger to dogs swimming in freshwater
more.summary: Diving into cool water can be a quick way to escape the summer heat, but during certain times of year, freshwater can pose hidden dangers to people and pets.

more.title: Europe's earliest glacier loss day in years signals a reckoning for the Alps
more.summary: On June 29, 2026, the snow accumulated by Switzerland's glaciers over the course of the previous winter had melted. Known as Glacier Loss Day, this date marks the point at which further melting begins to erode the glaciers' mass until snow accumulation resumes in the fall.

more.title: Textbooks may have misdrawn this basic brain structure for 100 years
more.summary: Scientists discovered that brain-cell axons may not be smooth tubes as textbooks have shown for more than a century, but instead naturally resemble strings of tiny pearls. Those pearl-like structures can change with neural activity and may help control how quickly electrical signals travel through the brain.

more.title: Circular economy pilot projects show hotels can reduce waste and costs
more.summary: The new EU Packaging Regulation (PPWR) has been in effect since Aug. 12, 2026. Under this regulation, beginning in January 2030, the food service industry may no longer buy food or toiletries packaged in single-use plastic—for example, ketchup packets or individually wrapped bars of soap. This is increasing pressure on hotels, restaurants and catering businesses to act.

more.title: Fossil plankton shells reveal reduced nitrogen fixation in warmer oceans 3 million years ago
more.summary: Nitrogen is a key nutrient because it fuels the growth of plankton, which forms the basis of the marine food web. Two opposing processes determine the global nitrogen cycle: nitrogen fixation and denitrification.

more.title: Report on global water resources: Worldwide continents are drying up
more.summary: The global water cycle is becoming increasingly unbalanced. Extreme droughts and floods are the result. This is shown in this year's report by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on the state of global water resources, "State of Global Water Resources 2025," which was published today.

more.title: Chemists overturn 40-year assumption about a key class of superconductors
more.summary: Scientists at Warwick have shown that a material treated for 40 years as a uniform, textbook superconductor is in fact a patchwork of different crystal structures throughout its bulk, using an advanced 3D imaging technique to see deep inside the crystal for the first time.

more.title: Transfer learning corrects alloy calculations to predict unexplored materials
more.summary: Metals can be transformed into alloys by adding different elements, allowing their strength, stability and other properties to be tailored. A key parameter for understanding these properties is the volume size factor (VSF), which quantifies lattice distortion caused by differences in atomic size.

more.title: Newfound fungal nutrient-sensing mechanism could advance biofuels and disease control
more.summary: Scientists have taken a step toward a better understanding of how fungi sense and respond to nutrients in the environment, which is critical for engineering fungi for green technologies and combating fungal pathogens and their resistance to treatments.

more.title: Motivational traits may help explain why some people report greater well-being
more.summary: "People who are determined, passionate and believe in their ability to improve appear more likely to flourish and experience meaningful, engaging lives," says Professor Hermundur Sigmundsson at NTNU's Department of Psychology.
